subject: Clarify DPA incident notice criteria & evidence handover — DataHealth request
messages:
From: Catherine Li <catherine.li@datahealth.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 21 Aug 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Possible data exposure affecting DH-prod — initial details

Hi Vanessa —

We detected unusual outbound traffic from one of our connector consumers that ingested tokens from DH-prod. Our SecOps team flagged a possible exfil event involving log exports and a subset of customer identifiers. We need to confirm whether Redwood observed an anomalous access pattern or retention misconfiguration on your side, and, critically, whether this meets the DPA definition of a "security incident" that triggers formal notice and evidence handover.

Two asks to start:
1) Please confirm the window of ingestion and any corresponding request/response logs you can share (redacted token values are fine).
2) Outline Redwood's DPA notice timeline and the expected format/transfer mechanism for evidence (SFTP? secure drive? escrow).

We appreciate urgent clarification—DataHealth has a regulatory reporting obligation and 72-hour clock to assess jurisdictional obligations.

Thanks,
Catherine
Security Operations
DataHealth Inc

Attachment: DH-internal-detection-log-snippet.txt (referenced)

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>

Cc: Catherine Li <catherine.li@datahealth.com>, DataHealth SecOps <secops@datahealth.com>
Date: Sat, 21 Aug 2027 09:34:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Possible data exposure affecting DH-prod — initial details

Folks — looping you in. Catherine, thanks for the heads-up. Summary of our immediate next steps from Redwood:

- I will confirm whether any service-side misrouting or API misconfiguration occurred in the stated window (we're already pulling request/response logs).
- Legal and Privacy will advise on DPA trigger criteria, notification timelines, and any redaction constraints.
- If we confirm an incident that meets the DPA definition, Redwood will provide a formal incident notice and evidence package; we need to agree on scope (logs, KV-cache slices, backup snapshots) and transfer channel.

Monica/Neha/Aditya — can you review the attached excerpt from our standard DPA (redwood_dpa_incident_excerpt.pdf) and the evidence matrix draft (evidence_requirements_matrix.xlsx)? Highlight any clauses or inbound requests from DataHealth that would require escalation (e.g., cross-border transfer limits, subprocessor involvement).

Catherine — for our intake: what exact identifiers do you want excluded from exports for privacy reasons (PII at rest, token payloads)? Also confirm preferred transfer mechanism and whether your legal team requires a formal non-disclosure addendum for the evidence handover.

I'll update in line as we have log pulls.

— Vanessa
Sr. Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference

From: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>, Catherine Li <catherine.li@datahealth.com>
Date: Sat, 21 Aug 2027 10:07:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Possible data exposure affecting DH-prod — initial details

Vanessa / team — quick legal read:

1) DPA trigger: Our DPA (section 6.2 in the attached excerpt) defines "security incident" as unauthorized access, exfiltration, or disclosure of Customer Data. If the DataHealth detection indicates unauthorized export, that meets the trigger.

2) Notice timeline: We commit to "prompt" notice and to provide an initial assessment within 72 hours of confirmation. We typically issue a formal notice letter within five (5) business days including preliminary scope and mitigation steps.

3) Evidence scope: We can provide request/response logs, auth traces, and configurable KV-cache snapshots. We will not provide raw customer token contents—those must be redacted or replaced with deterministic hashes unless DataHealth provides a lawful basis and redaction waiver. Backups older than 30 days require additional internal approvals.

4) Subprocessor coordination: If the evidence requires action from a subprocessor (cloud egress, logging vendor), we will coordinate but cannot force third-party disclosure beyond their contractual obligations. Expect an additional 3-7 business day delay for subprocessor evidence pulls.

5) Transfer mechanics: Standard options — secure SFTP to DataHealth-managed endpoint, temporary shared drive with tenant-level controls, or our Escrow partner (DocTransfer) under NDA. If DataHealth requires cross-border export, we need to document lawful transfer basis.

I'll prepare a draft incident notice and redaction matrix; Vanessa, can you confirm the ask list from Catherine so we align deliverables?

— Monica
Counsel, Privacy & Security
Redwood Inference

Date: Sat, 21 Aug 2027 12:01:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Possible data exposure affecting DH-prod — initial details

Thanks Vanessa/Monica — to be explicit on our requirements:

- We need an initial assessment (high-level yes/no on whether Customer Data was accessible or exported) within 24 hours if possible. Regulatory clock is tight in our EU customer set.
- For evidence we request: request/response logs (with request IDs), user-agent and source IPs, and delivery receipts (if any). We will accept deterministic hashes for token payloads but need a mapping for our internal five samples for triage.
- Transfer: preferably SFTP to our SecOps bucket. If you require an NDA or escrow, please provide a template and estimated turnaround.

Also: please confirm whether any subprocessor (e.g., logging provider LogRail Inc.) would need to be contacted and whether Redwood can act as liaison. If subprocessor involvement is required for logs older than 48 hours, that will affect timing.

Catherine

Catherine — thank you. Quick status update and commitments:

- Our runtime team confirms no anomalous outbound egress from Redwood-managed GPUs to unknown endpoints during the window reported. However, we did observe elevated API retries tied to a mis-tagged ingestion job (08:42–09:05 PDT) that caused duplicate writes to a transient logging bucket. We're treating that as potential scope.
- Per Monica's guidance, Redwood will: (a) produce an initial assessment within 24 hours (by 2027-08-22T09:12:00-07:00), (b) provide a formal incident notice within five business days if the assessment confirms a DPA-triggering incident, and (c) deliver an evidence package via SFTP endpoint subject to an evidence NDA.
- Evidence matrix (attached) shows which artifacts we can provide immediately (request/response logs with hashed payloads, auth traces) and which require subprocessor pull (older backups, third-party log archives). Estimated subprocessor pull timeline: 3–10 business days depending on provider SLA.

Next steps: Catherine, please send SFTP endpoint details and the list of five sample identifiers you want unhashed for triage under an evidence NDA. Monica/Neha/Aditya — I'll schedule a 30-minute sync for Monday to review the notice draft and handover checklist.

— Vanessa
Sr. Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference
